name: basic_commit_and_push
assertions: stages changed files with git add
creates a commit with a conventional commit message
pushes to the remote tracking branch
reports success with commit SHA and remote ref

name: ship_it_slang
assertions: recognizes 'ship it' as a commit-and-push intent
stages all relevant changed files
generates a conventional commit message from diff analysis
pushes to the current branch's upstream

name: push_my_changes
assertions: triggers the cp skill for push intent
commits any uncommitted work before pushing
pushes to the correct remote branch
does NOT create a pull request

name: negative_just_commit_no_push
input: just commit these changes, don't push
assertions: does NOT trigger the cp skill
recognizes the explicit no-push intent
performs a local commit only without pushing

name: negative_create_pr
input: create a PR for my feature branch
assertions: does NOT trigger the cp skill
recognizes PR creation as a different workflow
does NOT auto-push as part of PR creation

name: conventional_commit_message
input: commit and push the login form validation I just added
assertions: generates a conventional commit message (feat:, fix:, chore:, etc.)
commit message summarizes the actual diff content
commit message is concise (under 72 characters for subject line)
does NOT use generic messages like 'update files'

name: confidential_file_exclusion
assertions: excludes .env files from staging
excludes credentials.json and similar secret files
warns the user about skipped confidential files
stages only non-sensitive files for commit
does NOT silently include secrets in the commit

name: split_commits_mixed_files
input: ship all my work, I added new models and fixed a bug in the API
assertions: analyzes the diff to identify logically separate changes
creates separate commits for new features vs bug fixes
uses appropriate conventional commit prefixes (feat: vs fix:)
pushes all commits to remote in a single push
